description:
An experienced dwarven fighter in enchanted chain armor, now using a Battle axe with both hands. The original source inventory named Gauntlets of Ogre Power, Chain armor +1 and Long sword +1; the current saved loadout keeps Chain armor +1 and replaces the sword and gauntlets with the two-handed Battle axe. Source wealth remains 15 gp. This dwarf is rendered at a four-foot visual target within his 1x1 combat footprint.

IMAGEGEN PROMPT READY:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: OpenGold combat sprite MON6CHA.DAX:48/added_61186225371__two_hand/ready; exactly one transparent pixel-art frame.
Input image 1 is the NEW generated ready draft with this dwarf and is the edit target. Input image 2 is the earlier approved NEW ready sprite for the exact dwarf identity, chainmail, hands, feet, shaft position and camera. Input image 3 is the approved bipedal pose guide for front three-quarter screen-right facing/high guard only. No original game art is used.
The battle-axe head in Input 1 STILL LOOKS LIKE A CRESCENT OR SCYTHE. Fix that specific failure. Replace ONLY its metal head with a conventional SINGLE-BLADED BATTLE AXE: a thick cylindrical steel EYE/socket encircles the wooden haft, a SOLID FILLED broad trapezoid/wedge-shaped steel CHEEK projects to screen left, and a clearly exposed nearly straight or gently convex VERTICAL CUTTING EDGE forms the broad outer left side. The middle of the blade must be solid steel, not a black open crescent notch; do not draw upper/lower horns, a moon shape, sickle, halberd, scythe, double axe, or separated floating blade. Make the poll compact on the opposite side of the socket. At high resolution the steel cheek has substantial interior area all the way from the eye to the edge, so it remains visibly an axe when reduced to 128x128.
Keep the same full-length straight wooden haft across the dwarf's upper chest and behind his shoulder, both hands gripping that ONE shaft, same high ready guard, exact four-foot stout body, face, beard, Chain armor +1, belt, boots, stance, camera, palette and transparent canvas origin. No body/foot translation or change of grip. The 1x1 body footprint stays unchanged; raised axe may cross only the top tile line, and all pixels stay inside the transparent 128x128 canvas after common export. Exactly one dwarf and one frame, no duplicate, diptych, sheet, new gear, sword, shield, gauntlets, scenery, floor, shadow, text, border, black box or opaque background. Crisp pixel art and genuine alpha.

Input image 1 is the corrected FINAL 128x128 ready sprite; use it as the canvas and preserve its lower 65 pixels exactly, especially both boots and the chainmail skirt. Input image 2 is a rejected attack DRAFT that shows the desired straight-forward two-hand axe extension, but its body and boots have slid left. Use image 2 only to guide the shape of the upper arms and axe. Input image 3 is the approved bipedal pose guide for front three-quarter screen-right attack timing. No original game art is used.
Produce the action by editing image 1 in place. Lock every pixel from y=75 through y=127 to image 1. Keep the ready dwarf's head, beard, shoulders, chest, belt, hips, legs and both boot positions. Change his arms and the axe to the attack shown in image 2: BOTH hands grip one continuous wooden shaft, arms extend horizontally toward screen right at shoulder height, body leans modestly into the strike, steel battle-axe blade points straight forward toward screen right. Keep the actual axe a conventional single blade with a solid filled wedge and clear socket, not a crescent, scythe, halberd or hammer. Keep the blade entirely inside the 128x128 canvas with right margin and preferably around x=111..124. Preserve visible neck, chest, waist and pelvis continuity. The result must look like the SAME dwarf standing on the SAME two foot pixels between ready and action, while the far-back raised axe swings fully forward. Do not recenter or shrink the figure. Exactly one dwarf, one frame, no duplicate, diptych, sheet, new gear, sword, shield, gauntlets, scenery, floor, effect, motion blur, shadow, text, border, opaque background. Transparent pixel art.

ACCEPTED ACTION IMAGEGEN PROMPT (before transparent 128x128 registration):
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: OpenGold combat sprite MON6CHA.DAX:48/added_61186225371__two_hand/action; exactly one transparent pixel-art frame.
Input image 1 is the FINAL 128x128 corrected ready sprite of this exact dwarf, with solid wedge battle axe, and is the edit target. It defines the actual 128x128 canvas coordinates. Input image 2 is the approved bipedal pose guide for screen-right two-handed strike timing only. No original game art is used.
EDIT ONLY THE UPPER ARMS AND AXE OF INPUT 1. Copy every lower-body pixel below canvas y=75 from the ready image without ANY change: same belt, chainmail skirt, legs and both planted boots. Keep the dwarf's head/beard centered near canvas x=72..88,y=25..45, his torso centered near x=70,y=55 and both shoulders attached to that torso. Do not shift the character left, slide the feet, change size or camera, or move the head behind the pelvis. The action must read as the same character in place.
From the far-back ready guard, EXTEND BOTH HANDS and the full battle-axe STRAIGHT AHEAD toward screen right at chest-to-shoulder height. Both hands grip the SAME continuous wooden haft with space between the hands. The shaft projects horizontally right from the hands, and the SOLID single-blade wedge axe head sits near canvas x=112..123,y=45..65, fully inside the transparent image with margin. The thick eye/socket stays attached to the haft and the broad steel cutting edge faces SCREEN RIGHT. Make the two arms and shoulders visibly connected; lean the upper chest modestly right while tracing an unbroken neck/chest/waist to the fixed pelvis. This is a late forward blow, NOT a low chop, downward swing, crescent, scythe, spear, halberd, shovel, or detached blade. The axe may cross the 1x1 dotted tile boundary but NOT the PNG border.
Keep the four-foot dwarven fighter's beard, face, hair, Chain armor +1, belt, boots, colors, and front three-quarter screen-right camera. Saved gear is only chainmail and this two-handed battle axe. Exactly one dwarf, one action frame, no duplicate, diptych, sheet, shield, sword, gauntlets, scenery, floor, effect, motion blur, shadow, text, border, black box or opaque background. Crisp pixel art with genuine alpha.

The final pair uses canvas registration so both planted boots stay at the same combat coordinates. The later in-place edit prompt above was a rejected draft.
